trigger.description: Advisor A enters: 'The Smiths need $75,000 for their home renovation by August 15.' Simultaneously, advisor B enters a second $75,000 request for the same household (GC-11).
trigger.maskedRequestSummary: distribute 75000 USD for home-renovation; concurrent sibling request exists (tokenized)

householdEvidence.summary: Available balance 160000 USD. EITHER 75000 USD request alone leaves 85000 USD (>= the 48000 USD six-month reserve); both together would leave 10000 USD - a joint violation.
Planned withdrawals 8000 USD/month; Firm A six-month reserve = 48000 USD.
At this request's evaluation instant no sibling reservation exists yet - this request commits first.

typedQuantities.fromAssertedParse: no-pending-at-first-evaluation phrase (later postings are the execution tail)

expectedAuthority.note: 75000 USD exceeds Firm A's 25000 USD threshold: two distinct operations approvers, requester excluded.

expectedExecutionEligibility.reason: This request's reservation on conflict:smiths-liquidity commits FIRST; approvals recorded; revalidation confirms the reservation still holds and the sibling request cannot jointly violate the reserve.

expectedExplanationNodes.summary: A taxable source account was selected; a retirement account is never chosen silently.
After this movement the household still holds its policy-required months of planned withdrawals.
Alone, this 75000 USD movement preserves the 48000 USD reserve (160000 - 75000 = 85000).
The amount exceeds the firm's dual-approval threshold, so distinct approvers are required before execution.

commentaryNodes.summary: The liquidity conflict key for the household was free at commit time; this decision holds the reservation, making the joint constraint visible to every later evaluation.
